records.text: Grells are demonic creatures infesting Shadowglen and threatening its residents. Conservator Ilthalaine suspects the Fel Moss may have enchanted them, but the quest presents this as something to investigate, not a confirmed cause.

Grellkin are demonic creatures among the grells infesting Shadowglen and threatening its residents. Conservator Ilthalaine suspects the Fel Moss may have enchanted them, but the quest presents this as something to investigate, not a confirmed cause.

Tarindrella is a dryad and woodland protector who has returned to Shadowglen after years away from Kalimdor. Her return concerns the locals, and she is investigating a threat to the forest: she asks for Fel Moss to test whether it is corrupting the grells and grellkin. She fears the corruption may also have affected the Gnarlpine furbolgs and urges the player to consult Athridas Bearmantle in Dolanaar.
Greenpaw is a creature that fights with magic, casting Shock and using Rejuvenation when wounded.
Githyiss the Vile is a spider said to have bitten an explorer in a nearby spider cave, leaving them badly poisoned. The explorer asks a companion to seek help from Dirania Silvershine.
A Rascal Sprite encountered around the local woodland, it uses Faerie Fire in combat.
A Shadow Sprite found in the local woodland, it attacks in combat with Shadow Bolt.
A Dark Sprite of the local woodland, it uses Darken Vision in combat.
A Vicious Grell found in the local woodland, it fights with Savagery.
A Gnarlpine Ursa, a humanoid of Teldrassil.
A Gnarlpine gardener, one of several figures bearing that role.
A Gnarlpine warrior, one of the population’s combatants. This fighter can use a forceful attack in battle.
A Gnarlpine shaman who can call on Healing Wave in combat, especially when badly wounded.
A Gnarlpine defender, a fighter whose role is protection within the Gnarlpine population.
A Gnarlpine augur who brings curses into combat, including Curse of Weakness, and can strike with Gnarlpine Vengeance.
A Gnarlpine pathfinder, associated with finding routes for the population. This fighter can unleash Wrath in combat.
Gnarlpine Avenger is a Gnarlpine combatant whose technique is Gnarlpine Vengeance, used in combat.
Gnarlpine Totemic is a Gnarlpine combatant whose technique is Gnarlpine Vengeance, used in combat.
Bloodfeather Harpy threatens an attacking foe with talons, calls them easy prey, and boasts that their head will make a trophy.
Bloodfeather Rogue taunts an attacking foe as easy prey and threatens to shred them with talons or keep their head as a trophy.
Bloodfeather Sorceress threatens an attacking foe with talons and trophy-taking boasts; she also casts Frost Armor out of combat.
Bloodfeather Fury threatens a foe with talons, calls them easy prey, and boasts of taking their head as a trophy. It uses Savagery in combat.
A Bloodfeather Wind Witch is a hostile harpy who threatens prey with her talons and treats a defeated foe as a trophy. In combat, she uses gusts of wind.

A Bloodfeather Matriarch is a hostile harpy who threatens prey with her talons and treats a defeated foe as a trophy. In combat, she uses lightning, distinguishing her combat role from the Wind Witch’s gusts.
Timberling is an elemental creature.
The Timberling Bark Ripper is an elemental creature whose combat role includes a damaging spell.
The Timberling Trampler is an elemental creature whose combat kit includes a trample attack.

Lord Melenas is a satyr who has gathered grell warriors in a cave at Fel Rock, near Dolanaar. He is described as plotting something foul, though the nature of his plan is not given. His role in the local account is that of a dangerous, organized antagonist.

Ursal the Mauler is the beast Athridas Bearmantle blames for meddling with the Druids of the Talon's calling. Athridas says Ursal must be slain for his ritual to free the druids to be completed, and directs the player to Gnarlpine Hold.
The Ancient Protector is a giant found in Teldrassil and Darnassus.

Melithar Staghelm is concerned by Tarindrella's unexpected return to Shadowglen after years away from Kalimdor's forests. He has heard of her presence through the forest spirits and asks the player to learn what business brought her to the grove. He knows of her return, but the reason for it is unknown to him.

Athridas Bearmantle is responsible for the safety of the sleeping Druids of the Talon and grows uneasy when their protector’s report is delayed. He sees the Gnarlpine attacks and the missing Relics of Wakening as an urgent threat: without the relics and Ursal’s defeat, the druids remain trapped in sleep. He prepares to perform the awakening ritual himself.

Conservator Ilthalaine describes his purpose in Shadowglen as maintaining nature’s balance. After unusually heavy spring rains let nightsabers and thistle boars multiply beyond the forest’s food supply, he calls for a staged reduction of their populations: first the young animals, then the older ones. He regards killing them as a necessary cost of preserving the land for all who depend on it.

Denalan studies how Teldrassil's soil affects plants and timberlings. He prepares special soil to test whether seeds can grow into more docile timberlings, and investigates unusual finds such as a moss-covered timberling heart and exotic fruit that reacted strangely with the soil. He is troubled by the timberlings' anger and by corruption spreading around Lake Al'Ameth, and asks for help examining its causes and removing a source of it.

Sentinel Kyra Starsong is associated with the forest Council's demand that a character who aided Zenn Foulhoof redeem themselves. The Council condemns killing nature's creatures and calls for a lesson: give Foulhoof corrupted Fel Cones, which he may mistake for harmless food. The task reflects the Council's judgment and conditions for friendship with Teldrassil.

Gilshalan Windwalker is a night elf studying the Webwood spiders of Shadowthread Cave. He suspects the world tree has affected their venom, and seeks venom sacs and an unhatched egg to compare with smaller spiders and study the specimens. He plans to continue this work in Darnassus.

Syral Bladeleaf helps run Dolanaar’s busy herb and alchemy shop. Her husband spends so much time mixing potions that they have little time together, so she offers rare herbs in trade for prepared elixirs. She also passes along a delivery request for her colleague Denalan, who studies Teldrassil’s plant life.

Gaerolas Talvethren serves as Great Warden to the hibernating Druids of the Talon in Ban’ethil Barrow Den, protecting their safety and their pact with Ysera. Wounded after the Gnarlpine furbolgs ambushed him and pillaged Starbreeze Village, he reports their corruption and Ursal the Mauler’s use of Fel Moss. He welcomes help sent by Athridas Bearmantle.

Zenn Foulhoof is a satyr who recruits adventurers to gather animal parts and spider silk for his secret reagent business. He delights in having a naive recruit do his bidding when they bring the requested goods, and expects a harmless snack when they return with Fel Cones. When tricked, he protests that he has been duped by trickery.

Moon Priestess Amara is a Sentinel responsible for the road between Dolanaar and Darnassus, where Gnarlpine ambushers threaten travelers and the movement of news and trade. She calls for the attackers to be driven off and salutes those who serve the people of both settlements and Teldrassil.

Gnarlpine Ambushers are corrupted furbolgs of the Gnarlpine tribe who attack travelers on the road between Dolanaar and Darnassus. Their den lies below the nearby vantage point; they are an active threat to people using the route.

Sentinel Shayla Nightbreeze is a quest contact for the Forest Council's effort to make an adventurer who aided Zenn Foulhoof redeem themself. The task is to trick the satyr with Fel Cones, corrupted seeds that he will mistake for a harmless snack.
Agal is a humanoid found in Teldrassil.

Oakenscowl is a timberling that Denalan describes as spreading corruption among the creatures of Lake Al'Ameth. Denalan's account places it in a cave along the lake's southern bank and describes a huge tumor poisoning it.
An enslaved Druid of the Talon, whose words celebrate freedom after Ursal's nightmare ends: “The nightmare of Ursal is over! We are free!”
Keldas is a pet trainer who only helps hunters and their pets. He offers training for hunters to pass on to their pets.

Tenaron Stormgrip guides a lesson about the aftermath of the Battle of Mount Hyjal, explaining Nordrassil’s diminished state and the role of moonwells in druidic practice and Sentinel reverence. He sends the student to gather moonwell water and continue the account with Corithras Moonrage, framing the task as preparation to leave the forests of Teldrassil.

Corithras Moonrage continues Tenaron’s lessons on Teldrassil, explaining how moonwell water is collected and describing the aftermath of Nordrassil’s loss, Malfurion’s disappearance, and Fandral Staghelm’s leadership and plans for the new World Tree. His account also covers the dragons’ refusal to bless Teldrassil and its flawed, unpredictable growth. He also discusses the loss of immortality and reports furbolg attacks.

Sentinel Arynia Cloudsbreak was sent with other Sentinels to protect the Oracle Tree from harpies nesting around the Oracle Glade, and she has worked to drive them back. After a messenger carrying the tree's report was killed, she entrusted a new report to a traveler she believed could deliver it safely. Arynia also deeply cares for Mist, her faithful sabercat companion, and greets her with relief after the two are reunited.

Blackmoss the Fetid is an elemental whose heart is described as an unusual remnant: dark, oily moss covers it, yet it continues to beat slowly after its removal. That persistent rhythm is the clue by which the moss-covered organ can still be recognized as a heart.

Tallonkai Swiftroot is concerned with the emerald dreamcatcher given to him by Gaerolas Talvethen, a warden of the druids. He says the amulet draws energy from the Emerald Dream and has been stolen from his dresser at Starbreeze Village. He also asks for discretion about Lord Melenas, whose threat is close to home and an embarrassment to the night elves.

Mist is a badly wounded gray sabercat with bright blue eyes and an evident wish to follow. After being roused, she growls in acknowledgement and sets off into the forest. Her rescue is tied to an escort to Sentinel Arynia Cloudsbreak at the moon well near the Oracle Tree; her follow script reflects this specific reunion journey.

Teldrassil Sentinels serve as guides for visitors looking for places in Teldrassil. Their menu offers choices including the bank and the Rut’theran ferry, giving this sentinel a practical role in helping people find their way around the region.
Lyrai is a general supplies merchant in Teldrassil. Visitors can browse her goods, making her a practical source of general provisions for people passing through the area.
Khardan Proudblade is a weaponsmith in Teldrassil. His goods are available for visitors to browse, giving him a distinct role among the local suppliers: he deals in weapons.
Keina is a bowyer in Teldrassil, with goods available for visitors to browse. Her specialty is bows, distinguishing her trade from the other local merchants and smiths.
Janna Brightmoon is a clothier in Teldrassil. Her trade centers on clothing, giving visitors a local source for clothier goods alongside the area’s other specialist merchants.

Freja Nightwing is a leather armor merchant in Shadowglen. She offers goods to browse, and her local records also mark her as a questgiver; the available evidence does not identify a particular quest or personal history.
Andiss is Shadowglen’s armorer and shieldcrafter. Her local services include browsing goods and repairs, placing her among the village’s practical equipment providers.

Alyissia, Shadowglen’s warrior trainer, welcomes other races to the night elf home while advising that trust should be measured. She speaks of protecting her people amid the corruption of forest creatures and the changes following Teldrassil’s creation, and offers warrior instruction as people grow stronger.

Frahun Shadewhisper trains rogues in Shadowglen and sees peace with other races as fragile. He warns that Horde members may seek to deepen distrust, while urging his people to be prepared and protect their kind; his advice links learning to handle one’s chosen weapon with growing stronger.

Shanda trains priests in Shadowglen and offers instruction in Elune’s ways. Her welcome to new students reflects Teldrassil’s growing traffic, including Alliance visitors preparing for adventures. She encourages trainees to seek help from others in Shadowglen, return when they need training, and take care on the road.

Ayanna Everstride trains hunters in Shadowglen. She describes the hunter’s path as learning to tame beasts, use a bow accurately, and respect both the lands of the Kaldorei and those beyond. She warns that the world holds dangers greater than a novice might expect and urges hunters to value their animal companions. Her guidance sends new hunters onward to seek further instruction, including lessons in taming.

Mardant Strongoak mentors young druids in reading the spirits and understanding the Emerald Dream. He teaches that tranquility can be found through inner balance, even within a town's stone walls, and says deeper training in the Dream comes with growth.
Kyra Windblade teaches the art of war to aspiring warriors. She offers instruction to those suited to the warrior's path and can help them with their training.

Jannok Breezesong trains rogues, but his thoughts often turn to Syurna. He admits to spending his days thinking of her and filling his home with her portraits. Since she will speak only with rogues, he asks one to deliver her a rose from him.

Laurna Morninglight is a priest trainer in Dolanaar who teaches the ways of Elune. She says she is needed to train the other students, and directs a novice to aid the injured Sentinel Shaya nearby. Her instruction links priestly healing and fortitude with service to Elune; she thanks the novice for that service and welcomes them into the order.

Dazalar is a hunter trainer in Dolanaar whose taming lessons teach respect for nature and the differences among potential animal companions. His sequence moves from a spider to a nightsaber and then an owl; he describes the final lesson as preparation for taming and managing a chosen companion. His brief replies mark a novice's progress through the training.
Kal trains druids and offers talent untraining. He speaks of druids as preservers of the balance and urges them to keep Malfurion’s light alive while their master remains lost in the Dreaming.

Cyndra Kindwhisper is an alchemy trainer who worries that corruption is spreading even through Teldrassil. She voices the druids’ hope that nature will eventually drive the Horde from Kalimdor, and praises a student’s growing understanding of potions.
Malorne Bladeleaf teaches herbalism. His options also include talent and pet-skill untraining.
Nadyia Maneweaver trains leatherworkers. She advises making stitches smaller so fewer items slip from quivers and ammo pouches, and so tunics do not turn out lumpy.
Alanna Raveneye trains enchanting and keeps Elune’s many secrets close, saying they should not be shared with just anyone.
Androl Oakhand trains fishing. When a student's skill surpasses his, he points them toward Old Man Heming's book in Booty Bay; for further progress, he names Nat Pagle in Dustwallow Marsh.
Aldia is a general-supplies merchant. Her records offer browsing goods and identify her as a quest contact, though they do not establish the subject or outcome of any particular quest.
Shalomon is a weaponsmith in the settlement. His records offer weapons browsing and repair, placing his work with arms and their upkeep.
Jeena Featherbow is a bowyer. Her records offer browsing goods and repair, and mark her as a quest contact; they do not identify a particular quest or its outcome.
Brannol Eaglemoon is a clothier. His records offer goods browsing and repair, and identify him as a quest contact without establishing the subject or outcome of a particular quest.
Sinda sells leather armor. Her records offer goods browsing and repair, and identify her as a quest contact without establishing the subject or outcome of any particular quest.
Meri Ironweave is an armorer and shieldcrafter who offers goods for browsing and repairs equipment.
Narret Shadowgrove is a trade-supplies merchant whose goods are available to browse.
Vesprystus is the hippogryph master at Rut'theran Village. His gossip offers a ride and describes a hippogryph connection to Darkshore; when asked about transport, he asks whether you need a ride.
Nyoma sells cooking supplies in Dolanaar and welcomes visitors looking for recipes or basic cooking ingredients.
Danlyia is a food-and-drink vendor who offers goods for browsing.
Dellylah is a food-and-drink vendor who greets newcomers warmly and introduces herself by name.

Byancie is a first aid trainer. She points students to Doctor Gustaf VanHowzen in Theramore for further training and mentions Deneb Walker's book in Stromgarde as a way to improve their first aid techniques.

Vorlus Vilehoof is a satyr who defiled a remote moonwell southeast of Ban’ethil Barrow Den. Elanaria called him a threat to the moonwell and required his horn as proof of his defeat before she would begin advanced warrior training.

Zarrin is a cook who teaches both cooking and a Kaldorei lesson about living in balance with nature. She asks students to take only what they need and return in kind, and urges them to develop empathy for the living forests.
Radnaal Maneweaver is a skinning trainer.

Innkeeper Keldamyr welcomes travelers to the Dolanaar inn and urges them to rest and keep their strength and spirits. When Porthannius’s herb delivery arrives, Keldamyr regrets that his friend could not bring it himself, since they have much to discuss, but is glad to receive the herbs and meet the traveler.

Porthannius has business with the druids of Shadowglen that keeps him from carrying a package of herbs to Innkeeper Keldamyr in Dolanaar himself. He asks a traveler to deliver it; Keldamyr later says the two have much to discuss, showing a personal connection between them.
Melarith is a named individual found in Teldrassil.

Sethir the Ancient is a satyr who guards his home against intruders and sees corruption spreading through the forest. He calls for the forests to be cleansed, yet despairs that cutting down the growth only produces more. He believes the end of days is near and speaks of returning to the earth.

Ferocitas the Dream Eater is named as the leader of the Gnarlpine mystics. Tallonkai reports that Ferocitas wears a necklace glowing green at night and suspects it is the missing emerald from his damaged dreamcatcher.

The Gnarlpine mystics are a group Tallonkai describes as corrupted and places north of Starbreeze. Their leader, Ferocitas the Dream Eater, is linked in Tallonkai's account to a glowing green necklace suspected to be a stolen emerald. The mystics are targets in the search for the missing jewel.

Oben Rageclaw is a druid whose spirit is trapped in the Emerald Dream while Gnarlpine shamans use his animated body to attack intruders in the Ban’ethil Barrow Den. He asks for a shaman voodoo charm so he can understand the enchantment, then directs the player to kill his soulless body and use the charm to free him. He regrets asking for this and warns that the enchantment is powerful.
Rageclaw is a combatant in Teldrassil that can cast Bear Form and Maul.

Lady Sathrah is a named spider of Teldrassil, found near Wellspring Lake. She was once beloved of Elune; her silvery threads caught the evening mist, and their dew was kept at the Temple of the Moon for its healing powers. She later descended into madness, threatening her future generations. Priestess A’moora asks that her suffering be ended and her silvery spinnerets brought to the temple.

Daryn Lightwind is a Cenarion lore keeper whose studies range from Feralas history and ruins to wildlife and ancient elven sites. She is skeptical of Troyas Moonbreeze’s claims about his discoveries, reasoning that anything valuable in the ruins was likely taken long ago. She lends her book on Feralas history only after a favor, and has also studied the Hinterlands snapjaw Gammerita and the ruins of Winterspring.

Erelas Ambersky studies wildkin feathers to investigate their apparent magical qualities and whether the creatures are connected to Elune. Erelas compares feathers from different regions and remains curious about whether wildkin are ferocious monsters or misguided pets. Erelas also says that they train and cares for young hippogryphs, and describes this work as helping their population flourish.

Dirania Silvershine is worried when her friend Iverron misses his usual visit. After learning he has been poisoned by spiders, she says she knows an antidote that may help and asks for specific mushrooms, lilies, and spider ichor to prepare it. She emphasizes that the finished antidote remains viable for only five minutes, coordinating a hurried treatment.

Iverron was bitten and seriously poisoned by Githyiss the Vile while exploring the nearby spider cave. Dizzy and worried, he asks that Dirania Silvershine be told, trusting her to help. He says she often gets him out of trouble; after drinking the antidote, he feels better but asks for help clearing a path through the Webwood spiders.

Seriadne is a stable master who can help with pet stabling and lost companions. Her offered services include stable access and assistance recovering a lost companion; the available dialogue may depend on context.

Nessa Shadowsong sells fishing supplies in Rut'theran Village and is investigating why Teldrassil's coastal fish are unusually large and abundant. She suspects the new world tree may affect local wildlife and uses a courier to compare her findings with those of her colleague Laird in Auberdine.
Huntress Nhemai is a huntress found in Teldrassil.
Huntress Yaeliura is a huntress found in Teldrassil.
Orenthil Whisperwind welcomes visitors presenting a special Dolanaar gift voucher and offers a unique companion gift in exchange.
A sentinel of Shadowglen.
Sentinel Shaya was wounded while patrolling near Dolanaar. After receiving healing and a priest's blessing, she says she is ready to confront the corrupt timberlings with Elune's power behind her.
Uruson is a humanoid who can cast Demoralizing Roar in combat.
Grimmaw is a humanoid who can cast Vicious Bite in combat.
Duskstalker is a beast that can cast Tendon Rip.
Fury Shelda is a humanoid who can cast Deafening Screech in combat.
Threggil is a demon who can cast Strike in combat.

Elder Bladeleaf is an elder whose words look to the stars for hope and strength in the ages ahead, and suggest that the heavens may hold answers to earthly mysteries. Visitors can ask him where to find Elder Bladeswift or Elder Skygleam.

A quiet Forest Wisp that hums rather than speaking aloud, yet can communicate through thoughts. It bears a message concerning Tyrande and directs the listener onward to Keeper Remulos in Moonglade, following preparations by Shan'do Stormrage.

A Darnassus Reveler celebrating the Lunar Festival. The reveler praises the celebration and moon-powered fireworks, and explains the moonlight beam's destination. They also recognize that festival goodwill does not erase old hostilities between rival cities.
A spectral combatant that uses Scourge Strike.

A Teldrassil Flame Warden who welcomes visitors to honor the Alliance festival fires. The warden urges travelers to honor those fires across Alliance lands and openly encourages desecrating the Horde's fires, expressing a clear partisan hostility toward the rival festival.

place_records.text: You are in Teldrassil, Alliance land on the continent of Kalimdor. Dolanaar, Aldrassil and Rut'theran Village are its main settlements, and the Alliance keeps all three. Furbolgs, nightsabers, webwood spiders and bloodfeather harpies are its main dangers.

You are in Dolanaar, a town in Teldrassil. Its trainers teach warfare, roguery, the priesthood of Elune, hunting and druidism. Moon Priestess Amara, a sentinel on the road to Darnassus, says Gnarlpine ambushers threaten travelers there and disrupt the flow of news and trade.

You are in Shadowglen, in Teldrassil. Conservator Ilthalaine keeps the balance of the forest here, and after heavy spring rains he calls for nightsabers and thistle boars to be reduced. Grells, demonic creatures, infest the grove, and the dryad Tarindrella, back after years away, is investigating whether Fel Moss is corrupting them. Dirania Silvershine is anxious for her friend Iverron, who was poisoned by spiders.

You are in Aldrassil, in Teldrassil. Shanda trains priests and Ayanna Everstride trains hunters, and Ayanna warns that the world holds dangers greater than a novice might expect. Gilshalan Windwalker studies the Webwood spiders of Shadowthread Cave and suspects the world tree has changed their venom. Khardan Proudblade sells weapons and Keina sells bows.

You are in Lake Al'Ameth, a lake in Teldrassil. Denalan studies how the soil here affects plants and timberlings, and the timberlings around the lake have turned angry. Oakenscowl, a timberling in a cave on the southern bank, is spreading corruption to the creatures that make the lake their home.

You are in Starbreeze Village, in Teldrassil. Gnarlpine furbolgs pillaged it, and Gnarlpine warriors, gardeners and ursas still roam the village. Their chieftain Ursal the Mauler is said to be driven mad by Fel Moss. Gaerolas Talvethren, the Great Warden of the hibernating Druids of the Talon, was wounded in the ambush.

You are in Gnarlpine Hold in Teldrassil, held by Gnarlpine pathfinders, avengers and totemics. Ursal the Mauler and Grimmaw are the notable hostile ones here, and an enslaved Druid of the Talon is held in the hold.

You are in the Oracle Glade in Teldrassil, where sentinels guard the Oracle Tree against harpies nesting all around the glade. Bloodfeather rogues, matriarchs and wind witches are the harpies, and giant Webwood spiders and feral nightsabers roam there. Alanna Raveneye teaches enchanting.
You are in Wellspring River in Teldrassil, where elder timberlings and timberling mire beasts are the dangers. Blackmoss the Fetid is the notable hostile one.
You are in Wellspring Lake in Teldrassil. Timberling tramplers, webwood silkspinners and elder nightsabers are the hostile creatures found here.
You are in the Pools of Arlithrien in Teldrassil, where Gnarlpine defenders and shamans, nightsaber stalkers and webwood venomfangs are the dangers.

You are in Rut'theran Village, a fishing village in Teldrassil. Nessa Shadowsong sells fishing supplies and is studying why the fish along this coast are so large and plentiful. Vesprystus, the hippogryph master, keeps the village's flights, and Androl Oakhand trains fishing.
You are in Ban'ethil Hollow in Teldrassil, where Gnarlpine shamans, defenders, ambushers and augurs are the dangers. Agal and Rageclaw are the notable hostile ones there.
